fact: The Puntland education ministry's programme document of May 2022 states that the Digital Attendance Application, piloted by several education NGOs in Puntland in 2019, is currently being trialled in 42 schools, that state-wide collection of attendance data is not yet in place and that the Puntland EMIS is still under development; it gives Puntland 794 primary schools but does not say what level the 42 are, and the figure is for Puntland State only, not Somalia.

The Puntland education ministry's programme document of May 2022 states that the Digital Attendance Application collects daily student and teacher attendance on mobile devices, offline where needed, and uploads it to the Puntland EMIS server, giving attendance and drop-out data in real time; head teachers are to be trained to use it on tablets, and it is to track whether each supported child reaches 80% attendance.

The Puntland education ministry's programme document of May 2022 puts the roll-out of the Digital Attendance Application to its target schools (tablets, solar chargers, head teacher training) under a US$3.35 million GPE accelerated funding programme running May 2022 to April 2023 with UNICEF as grant agent, and calls the Puntland EMIS it feeds GPE-supported; no domestic funding is stated.

The Puntland education ministry's programme document of May 2022 states that the ministry proposes to expand the Digital Attendance Application, an open-source application first developed by UNICEF in Kenya and adapted and integrated with the ministry's EMIS, and assigns the collection and analysis of its attendance data to the ministry, with roll-out, training and technical support shared with a software company.

World Vision's annual report for 2019 states that it, the Somalia Response Innovation Lab and the Puntland Ministry of Education are piloting a Digital Attendance App in 3 primary schools in Puntland, a pilot it calls ongoing; it gives no total of schools, and the figure is for Puntland only.

World Vision's annual report for 2019 states that the 3 pilot schools moved from a paper attendance tracker to the app, which records each student's attendance daily, online or offline, with reasons for absence, and feeds each school's data into district and state figures broken down by school, gender and grade.
World Vision's annual report for 2019 states that the Digital Attendance App pilot in Puntland is in 3 primary schools.

World Vision's annual report for 2019 states that World Vision and the Response Innovation Lab worked with the software firm Sisitech to pilot the app in Puntland in collaboration with the Ministry of Education, that World Vision, head teachers and the government can see its dashboards, and that the ministry would like the app and its EMIS integrated, which they were not yet.
